source.title: Online Second Order Methods for Non-Convex Stochastic Optimizations

record.tranche_reason: Reports an outcome for large minibatch training, but does not state whether epochs were held fixed or give a detailed comparison recipe.
record.gate_note: Optimizer comparisons are reported, but the text does not state a direct SGD-versus-adaptive-optimizer result. Other optimizer and generalization findings in the paper do not test the listed versions. The large-batch result is an aggregate across unspecified benchmark problems.
record.test_reason: The large-batch statement does not identify held-out performance, a smaller-batch baseline, or a fixed epoch budget, so it cannot establish a result on V5. The stated optimizer outcomes compare PSGD with first-order methods rather than establishing the adaptive-versus-SGD generalization comparison in V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases Section V-D but omits the paper's main conclusion: PSGD, particularly with Kronecker-product or SCAN preconditioners, improves convergence and benchmark performance relative to the tested first-order methods. The batch-size statement does not establish a fixed-epoch held-out comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Compares PSGD and first-order methods on selected optimization benchmarks; the large-batch statement gives no fixed-epoch comparison recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that mini-batch size 1024 produced no meaningful performance loss; other batch-size conditions and their outcomes are not specified.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report no meaningful performance loss when trying batch size 1024 with PSGD, without specifying the outcome measure, comparator, or training budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PSGD can operate at batch size 1024 on the authors' benchmarks without an unspecified performance loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Kronecker-product PSGD achieves about 0.4% MNIST test error and slightly below 10% CIFAR-10 test error; the authors emphasize its advantages over first-order methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kronecker-product PSGD provides favorable convergence and held-out performance on these benchmark architectures.

record.problems: The large-batch statement does not identify the benchmark problems, comparison batch size, training budget, or a numerical measure. Training and testing curves are figures, and the text does not give exact values for optimizer comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-version results were stated as explicit outcomes. Comparisons among optimizers in the figures are not extracted as precise results because the text does not give their individual values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting compared with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
An interpretable adaptive-versus-SGD held-out comparison under a specified tuning budget; the supplied figure text does not establish this ranking.
Large-versus-small-batch held-out performance under fixed epochs and the effects of recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test accuracy after removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The optimizer curves are declared in rows_left_out. Their individual method rankings cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text. No verdict should be inferred from the missing batch-budget information.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected network comparison.
Direct adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out comparison.
Fixed-epoch comparison and the effects of longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, and regularization.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
